newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up, select blue chips lead.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up, select blue chips lead.

text.p: Selective strength in some major blue chips drove Hong Kong stocks to a higher close on Thursday, but brokers said the overall tone during the session had been fairly subdued ahead of the holiday period.
The Hang Seng index closed on a gain of 80.54 points at 12,846.56. Turnover was HK$7.19 billion compared with HK$6.29 billion on Wednesday.
"People are looking around for value," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
He pointed to a rise in HSBC Holdings shares which closed HK$2.00 higher at HK$157.00.
Hutchison was also a strong performer on Thursday, rising HK$1.25 to HK$58.00, while Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$1.25 to HK$92.00.
Brokers said a drop in Tokyo stocks had weighed on share prices during the day. The Hang Seng reached a low of 12,781.32 during the session.
The Nikkei 225 fell 522.36 points on Thursday to 19,570.67, its lowest close this year.

An overnight rise in the U.S. long bond yield was also a concern, with investors uncertain about the future direction of interest rates, brokers said. The benchmark 30-year treasury bond fell 16/32 overnight to yield 6.70 percent.

"The bond yield keeps coming up and I think people have quite different views on interest rates," said Amy Wong, research director at New China Hong Kong Securities. "I believe the market will be range trading before the closing of 1996."
But Wong said investors were optimistic about the Hong Kong market going into 1997.
"We are expecting a recovery in the Chinese economy and that will spread over into Hong Kong as well. We still expect a good 1997 ," she said.
Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities, said the Hang Seng had found solid support around current levels. "I think 12,800 to 13,000 will be the range" in the short term, he said.
December Hang Seng futures rose 40 points to 12,860.
